standard.title: Initiate and sustain exchanges in familiar contexts
standard.description: initiate and sustain modelled exchanges in familiar contexts related to students' personal worlds and school environment
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can initiate exchanges and respond to modelled questions about self, others and classroom environment (AC9LS4C01). They use formulaic expressions and modelled structures. They have not yet sustained exchanges beyond information exchange — including expressing feelings, opinions, preferences and using conversational maintenance strategies.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students initiate and sustain modelled exchanges in familiar contexts — including sharing personal information, expressing feelings and opinions, and using strategies to maintain conversational flow.

nodes.label: Expressing feelings, emotions and opinions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can express feelings, emotions, preferences and opinions in the target language — going beyond information exchange to personal response.
nodes.minimum_width: Express at least two feelings or emotions and at least one preference or opinion using appropriate target language structures.
nodes.typical_width: Express feelings and emotions about experiences; express preferences and opinions with supporting reasons; apologise and express concern or sympathy; use appropriate register for formal and informal contexts; share personal information about hopes and future plans.
wider: Express a nuanced emotional response — not only a simple feeling but an explanation of why, connected to a specific experience
Compare how opinions and preferences are expressed differently in the target language and English — identify where the target language requires more explicit grammatical marking
nodes.hinge_reason: Moving beyond information exchange to expressing feelings and opinions is the developmental leap between 3-4 and 5-6. Students who can only exchange factual information cannot sustain exchanges about personal worlds and cannot reach the opinion and negotiation demands of subsequent standards.

response_modes.reason: Expressing feelings and opinions requires a bank of structures across emotional and evaluative domains. Students need varied practice expressing feelings about different experiences before this vocabulary becomes spontaneously available.

success_criteria: Expresses at least two different feelings or emotions using correct target language structures
Expresses at least one preference or opinion with a supporting reason or elaboration

nodes.label: Sustaining exchanges using conversational strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can sustain a modelled exchange using conversational strategies — showing interest, asking follow-up questions and using fillers and reaction expressions.
nodes.minimum_width: Sustain an exchange for at least four turns using at least two different conversational strategies.
nodes.typical_width: Use conversational maintenance strategies — asking follow-up questions, using fillers and acknowledgement expressions, showing reactions; sustain exchanges using modelled conversation patterns; use target language for expressing agreement, disagreement and interest.
wider: Sustain an exchange on an unexpected topic — using maintenance strategies to keep the conversation going without preparation
Analyse a recorded exchange and identify every maintenance strategy used — categorise by type and evaluate which were most effective

response_modes.reason: Conversational sustainability develops through varied partner and topic conditions. Maintenance strategies need to transfer across varied topics and partners before they become genuinely available conversational tools.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Genuine conversational sustainability distinguishes rehearsed performance from authentic interaction. Width investment here produces the oral fluency dimension that matters most for real communication.
success_criteria: Sustains an exchange for at least four turns using at least two conversational strategies
Uses at least one reaction expression or filler that shows genuine response to a partner's contribution
